title: a conditional receiver that names two different capabilities does not identify one nominal key, and is refused rather than silently charged to one of them
notes: specification/requirements.mdx, 'Context Access': 'The receiver MUST identify a `Context` subclass strongly enough for the compiler to record its nominal key.' This program's receiver identifies two, so there is no key to record and the only closed answer is refusal. WHY THIS EXACT PROGRAM AND NOT THE OBVIOUS ONE: the obvious spelling of this case would pair two structurally DIFFERENT capabilities, and before 2026-08-26 that spelling merely produced an empty row — bad, but visibly bad. Reader and Writer here declare the same member with the same signature ON PURPOSE, because TypeScript subtype-reduces `typeof Reader | typeof Writer` to `typeof Reader`: nothing left in the receiver's TYPE remembers Writer. The measured consequence on the pre-fix tree was worse than an empty row and is the reason this case exists: both backends recorded `requirements: [Reader]`, `Layer.succeed(Reader, service)` satisfied that row exactly, the program was certified `ok: true` — and `readEither(false, ...)` reads Writer at run time and dies with `Panic: capability 'Writer' was not provided`. A MISATTRIBUTED row is certified by every downstream rule the row feeds: Layer completeness, transitive caller rows, and the top-level unsatisfied-requirement check. The layer and the `false` argument are therefore load-bearing parts of the case, not scenery: they are what make the row's wrongness reachable rather than theoretical. This also fixes the ordering a correct implementation must use — the branches have to be read out of the `?:` SYNTAX, because the checker's type for the receiver has already lost one of them. `structurally-identical-contexts-are-distinct-requirements` is this case's direct sibling and pins the same nominal-identity rule for two DIRECT receivers; it cannot see this defect, because a direct receiver never loses a constituent. WHAT THIS CASE DELIBERATELY DOES NOT PIN: the diagnostic message. `SMITHERS2106` carries a fixed sentence with no payload on either backend — there is no capability name, no row rendering, nothing a wrong-but-plausible refusal could get wrong — so `messageContains` would add no promise and would freeze wording that is explicitly not the contract. It also does not pin the SECOND diagnostic a reader might expect: no `SMITHERS2101` for an unsatisfied Writer, because a receiver that pins no key contributes no row to be unsatisfied. VERIFIED LOAD-BEARING, not assumed: mutating the declared column from 10 to 11 turns the case red on BOTH backends with the position diff printed, and the file was restored byte-identically (sha256 cca4aa3e8c3000b6baeeb469d4d30518225c1c37b4734f93b7c107965be099cf before and after). The paired positive control is `sound-capability-receivers-keep-their-row-and-run`, which spells `(flag ? Reader : Reader)` and `(flag ? Reader : Alias)` among thirteen sound receivers and must keep compiling AND RUNNING, so a branch walk that refuses every conditional receiver turns that case red instead of passing quietly.
